title: Science Equipment: The Compound Microscope
competency: Identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope.
objectives: Identify the mechanical, illuminating, and magnifying parts of a compound microscope.
Explain the function of each part of the microscope.
Demonstrate the correct way to carry and store a microscope.
Calculate the total magnification of a specimen.
introduction: The human eye is amazing, but it cannot see the tiny cells that make up our bodies. To enter the 'microscopic' world, scientists use a Compound Microscope. Learning how to use this tool correctly is the first step in becoming a biologist.
content:
1. Three Main Groups of Parts

The parts of a microscope are grouped based on their purpose:

  • Magnifying Parts: These make the specimen look larger. Includes the Eyepiece (Ocular) and Objectives.
  • Illuminating Parts: these control the light. Includes the Mirror or Light Source, Diaphragm, and Condenser.
  • Mechanical Parts: These support and adjust the microscope. Includes the Base, Arm, Stage, and Adjustment Knobs.

2. Key Parts and Functions

  • Eyepiece: The part you look through (usually 10x magnification).
  • Objectives: Lenses near the specimen (Scanner, LPO, HPO, and OIO).
  • Coarse Adjustment Knob: Moves the stage up and down for initial focusing.
  • Fine Adjustment Knob: Used for sharp, detailed focusing.
  • Stage: The flat platform where the slide is placed.

3. Handling and Care

Microscopes are expensive and delicate. Follow these rules:

  • Carrying: Always use two hands. One hand holds the Arm, and the other supports the Base.
  • Cleaning: Use only lens paper to clean the lenses. Tissue paper or cloth can scratch them.
  • Storage: Always rotate the nosepiece so the lowest power objective (Scanner) is in place before putting it away.

examples.title: Calculating Magnification
examples.description: To find the total magnification, multiply the Eyepiece power by the Objective power. (Example: 10x Eyepiece × 40x HPO = 400x Total Magnification).

keyTerms.definition: The ability to make an object appear larger.
The ability to distinguish between two points as separate objects (clarity).
The small piece of material being examined under the microscope.

keyConcepts: The compound microscope uses two lenses to produce an enlarged image.
Proper focusing always starts with the lowest power objective.
Light must pass through the specimen for it to be visible.
summary: The compound microscope is an essential tool in life science. By mastering its parts—from the magnifying lenses to the mechanical adjustment knobs—and practicing proper handling, students can explore the fundamental units of life.

selfCheck.q: Which part of the microscope do you use to sharpen the image under high power?
How should you carry a microscope?
selfCheck.a: With two hands: one on the arm and one under the base.

selfCheck.q: If the eyepiece is 10x and the objective is 10x, what is the total magnification?
